blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — mannitol mechanism for increased intracranial pressure
stem: A nurse reviews the action of intravenous mannitol prescribed to reduce increased intracranial pressure. Which mechanism best explains this effect?

options.A: Mannitol raises extracellular and plasma osmolarity, shifting intracellular water into extracellular and vascular compartments and thereby reducing intracranial edema and pressure.
options.B: Mannitol directly repairs the structural brain lesion causing intracranial hypertension, restoring damaged neural tissue and eliminating the source of cerebral edema.
options.C: Mannitol lowers plasma osmolarity so water moves from the vascular compartment into brain tissue, reducing circulating volume and relieving intracranial pressure.
options.D: Mannitol primarily suppresses cerebrospinal-fluid production through carbonic-anhydrase inhibition rather than producing an osmotic shift of tissue water.

rationale: Current mannitol labeling states that intravenous mannitol increases extracellular osmolarity and induces movement of intracellular water into extracellular and vascular spaces. This osmotic action underlies its role in reducing intracranial pressure and intracranial edema. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize that intravenous mannitol reduces intracranial pressure by increasing extracellular/plasma osmolarity and shifting intracellular water into extracellular and vascular compartments.
source_version_date: Current DailyMed label published in 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §12.1 Mechanism of Action: IV mannitol increases extracellular osmolarity, moving intracellular water to extracellular and vascular spaces; this action reduces intracranial pressure and edema.
source_claim_supported: Mannitol reduces intracranial pressure through an extracellular osmotic gradient that draws intracellular water into extracellular and vascular spaces.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: understand medication mechanism and therapeutic response during acute neurologic therapy.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all options as complete mechanistic explanations with comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current mannitol labeling; no second answer or residual length cue remains.
